description: The address's call and its charge (the line naming what the speech is about), written by the call-and-charge writer under the Story lead's spec (docs/story/writer-spec.md).

slots.term-left: the time left in the speaker's term, in words ("four years"), from the term's record
slots.theme-name: the speech's theme said as people say it (speech-outlines.json themeNames), from the planner's theme
slots.run-span: how long the economy's run lasted, in words, from the macro months (address-story.ts)
slots.the-disaster: the year's worst declared disaster as people say it after 'the' (outlines.json disasterWords), from the national events engine's row
slots.about: the policy question's spoken noun phrase (question-names.json)
slots.to: the policy question's spoken verb phrase
slots.law-name: the law in force or proposed, named (question-names.json law)
slots.other-side: what the other side of the speaker's stand wants done, as a verb phrase
slots.belief: the speaker's reason on the question, as a clause (question-names.json reasons)
slots.belief-sentence: the same reason as its own sentence
slots.today: how the question stands today, said from the speaker's side, as a sentence
slots.today-clause: the same, as a clause that ends the sentence
slots.the-vice-president: the Vice President by office and name, from the officials engine's seat
slots.president: the President, said by the said-as reader (role first, then pronoun)
slots.president-object: the President in the object case
slots.said: what the President's point was about, as people say it
slots.employer: the speaker's employer, through the said-as reader
slots.born-year: the year the player was born, from the birth record
slots.school-year: the year the player first started school
slots.school-place: the town the player first went to school in
slots.moved-year: the year the player's household moved
slots.finished-year: the year the player finished high school
slots.college-year: the year the player started college
slots.lost-office: the office the player ran for and lost, as people say it
slots.lost-votes: the player's votes in it, as a number
slots.state: the player's state, as a sentence says it
slots.president-name: the President's full name, from the officials engine
slots.we: the household members who watched and the player, as the subject of a sentence ("Joe, Ann and I")
slots.us: the same, as its object ("Joe, Ann and me")
slots.name: the person's full name, from the record
slots.surname: the person's family name, from the record
slots.date: the day as a news story says it
slots.quote: the line of the address a reader can quote, from the address's record
slots.body: the body that voted, as its record names it
slots.law: the bill or law by its name, never its number
slots.purpose: what the bill does, as a noun phrase from the bill catalog
slots.count: the vote count in words and figures ("3 to 2")
slots.body-word: the body the governor reports to, said as people say it after 'the' ("legislature"), from the speech's facts
slots.realm-name: the state, as the speech names it, from the speech's facts

parts.text: Most of what I have to say today is about {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I didn't run to keep a chair warm. What I came to talk about is {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: And I'm asking every one of you to talk with a neighbor who sees {theme-short} differently than you do.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Talk with a neighbor who sees {theme-short} differently than you do, and really listen.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: If you think I'm wrong about {about}, tell me. Better to hear it from you than from a poll.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Write to Congress about {about}. They read the mail more than they let on.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Run for something in your own town. The next {term-left} need more of you than one office in Washington.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Vote in the next election too. Congress decides what happens to {about} as much as I do.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: If you have work, help somebody find some. That's how we turn around the last {run-span}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: If you remember one thing from today, make it {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I'm going to spend most of my time up here on {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: There's one thing I ran on more than anything else, and it's {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You'll hear me talk about {theme-name} until you're tired of it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The first thing on my desk is {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I want to talk about {theme-name}, because it's what I heard about most on the road.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Let me get right to {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Go to a meeting where people argue about {theme-short}, and say what you think.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Find out who represents you in Congress before the week is out, and tell them where you stand on {about}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Pick one thing in your town that's broken and help fix it. That's how the next {term-left} go well.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Don't wait for me to fix {theme-short}. Some of it starts on your own street.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: When we argue about {theme-short}, remember your neighbors mostly want what you want.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Read what's in the bills on {theme-short}, not just what people say is in them.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Give a few hours this year to something in your town. The next {term-left} need it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Keep an eye on what Washington does about {theme-short}, and say so when we get it wrong.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Start with your own block. Whatever we do on {theme-short} in Washington lands there first.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: My first job is {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Before anything else today, I want to talk about {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I'll be brief about most things today, but not about {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Nothing I say today matters more than {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: When I asked people what kept them up at night, they told me about {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I came here to get one thing moving first, and that's {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Ask me what this job is about, and I'll tell you: {theme-name}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: There's a lot on the list, and {theme-name} is at the top.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Ask your kids what they think about {theme-short}. They'll be living with what we decide.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Keep your patience with each other. We're going to disagree about {theme-short} a lot in {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Check on somebody who's having a harder time than you. That's how the next {term-left} start right.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Vote in your local elections too. A lot of what touches {theme-short} gets decided there.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Be fair to the people you disagree with on {about}. I'll try to be fair to you.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Which question comes first? For me it's {theme-name}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Plenty of people asked me about {theme-name}, and I owe them an answer today.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Whatever you think of {about}, take a minute to learn what the other side is afraid of.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Show someone younger how to find their polling place. They'll be voting long after these {term-left} are over.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Tell the people who disagree with you about {about} one thing they got right.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Who here has talked about {theme-name} at a kitchen table? That's who I'm speaking to.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: We'll take on plenty in the next {term-left}. We'll start with {theme-name}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Let's spend the first stretch of this term where the trouble is: {theme-name}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The people I met kept coming back to {theme-name}, so I'm coming back to it too.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Here's the order I'll work in: {theme-name} first, everything else behind it.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: What brought me to this podium was {theme-name}, and that hasn't changed.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Where do I start? With {theme-name}, because it won't wait for a better time.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Every president has something to get to first. Mine is {theme-name}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I won't pretend everyone backs {about}. Meet the doubters halfway and listen to them.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: If {about} would cost you something, say so early, while it can still change.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Ask the next candidate who comes by where they stand on {about}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Don't let {theme-short} become something only experts talk about.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Whoever you trust on {theme-short}, check their work.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I'll make mistakes in the next {term-left}. Tell me early, and kindly if you can.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The last {run-span} were hard on a lot of homes. Make room at your table for someone who had it worse.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Whatever comes in the next {term-left}, I'll face it as someone who swore to do right by all of you.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I've sworn to the Constitution, not to a party, and I'll hold to that for {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: {the-vice-president} and I both took the oath today, and both of us answer to you for {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Last fall's election gave me {term-left} to show you what I meant.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Everything I said last fall now has to hold up over {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Rent, gas and groceries have all gone up over the last {run-span}, and you didn't need me to say so.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: For {run-span}, everything on the shelf has cost a little more than it should, and families have felt it.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The cost of living has crept up for {run-span}, and it's the first thing people raise with me.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Good jobs have been harder to find for {run-span}, and everyone here knows someone who's felt it.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: For {run-span}, too many people have been sending out applications and hearing nothing back.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: If the last {run-span} have worn you down, you aren't imagining it.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Nobody had an easy time of it these past {run-span}, and anyone who says otherwise wasn't paying attention.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Hiring has picked up over the last {run-span}, and more of you are getting that phone call.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Fewer people are out of work now than {run-span} ago, and that's your doing as much as anyone's.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Raises have been coming through for {run-span}, and you can see it at the end of the month.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: A lot of you have felt a little more breathing room over the last {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Families are still putting their lives back together after the {the-disaster}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Neighbors have spent this past year helping each other recover from the {the-disaster}, and the federal government ought to be helping too.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I'm thinking today about everyone the {the-disaster} touched.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Some towns haven't had one calm month since the {the-disaster}, and I won't ask them to be patient forever.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Whatever else is on our agenda, the {the-disaster} is not behind us.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Somewhere right now, a family is eating dinner in a rented room because of the {the-disaster}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Imagine a shop owner standing in the store the {the-disaster} emptied, deciding whether to unlock the door again.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: A neighbor showed up with a truck and a toolbox after the {the-disaster}, and asked for nothing back.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: A school bus is still taking the long way around the damage from the {the-disaster}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: To the people who didn't vote at all: I'm your President too, and I'll earn your attention over {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: To the people who disagree with me, and there will be many: I'll listen to you for all {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: To the survivors of the {the-disaster}: help is a job of this office, not a favor.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Plenty of people stopped making plans during the last {run-span}, and I want them making plans again.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Putting something back on the shelf has become a habit for a lot of families over {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I've heard from people out of work for {run-span} who still haven't given up, and I admire that.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The help-wanted signs went up over the last {run-span}, and people have been walking in.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: For {run-span}, a steady job has been easier to land than it used to be.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Take-home pay has been on the rise for {run-span}, and families have noticed.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: After {run-span} of steady raises, people are planning again.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: You've worked hard for {run-span}, and it has begun to show in your pay.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Plenty of families are saving a little again, after {run-span} of better pay.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Not everyone has felt the same lift, but most households are better off after the last {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Over {run-span}, pay has gone up in most trades and in most towns.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Let me start with the good news: pay has been climbing for {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Hiring and wages both moved the right way for {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I'd call the last {run-span} a good stretch for anyone who wanted work and a fair wage.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I'd be foolish to pretend the last {run-span} went badly, because for most of you they didn't.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: No one should have to ask twice for help, and over {term-left} I'll see that they don't.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The recovery gets a place in every plan I make for the next {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: People have switched brands, skipped trips and put off repairs for {run-span}, and that adds up.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Everyday things cost more today than they did {run-span} ago, and everyday people are the ones paying.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I know there are families here who have been without a paycheck for part of the last {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: People who've worked all their lives found themselves starting over in the last {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: A lot of people stopped expecting things to get better during the last {run-span}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Employers started hiring again, and for {run-span} they haven't stopped.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: To the workers who've been steady through {run-span} of uncertainty: thank you.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I'll start with {theme-name}, because it's what people raise with me most.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Of everything on my list, {theme-name} has waited the longest, so it goes first.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Why {theme-name}? Because it reaches more households than most things on my desk.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: When people ask what this administration is for, I start with {theme-name}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I ran on {theme-name}, and I'm going to begin there.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I'm putting {theme-name} first because waiting won't fix it.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Most of the work ahead depends on getting {theme-name} right, so I'm starting there.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Before anything else in the next {term-left}, I'll deal with {theme-name}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Read the text of a bill on {about} before you pass along anyone's opinion of it.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Look up how your own representatives voted on {about}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Go to a public meeting about {theme-short}, even if you never speak.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Learn the names of the people who run your town, because over the next {term-left} they'll make decisions that touch you every week.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Pick a local race in the next {term-left} and learn who's running before you decide.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: Make a habit of reading your local paper, or its website, over the next {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: If the last {run-span} were good to you, tell a friend who's still looking for work what helped.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: If you know someone who lost work in the last {run-span}, ask if you can introduce them to someone who's hiring.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The oath names the Constitution and nothing else. That's what I'll answer to for {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: I've taken the oath, so the next {term-left} are about the Constitution first and my own preferences second.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: The oath doesn't mention a party. It mentions the Constitution, and I'll work under it for {term-left}.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: You picked me in November for {term-left}, and I take that as a reason to listen to the ones who didn't vote for me.
parts.author: the call-and-charge writer

parts.text: To the voters who backed someone else: you'll get the same hearing from my office as anyone, over {term-left}.
